results.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust (Version 2)
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against a bench, knees bent, and feet flat on the floor. Place a dumbbell across your hips, holding it with both hands for stability.
Press through your heels to lift your hips upward until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Hold the top position for a moment, ensuring your glutes are fully contracted.
Lower your hips back down to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Press through your heels to maximize glute activation.
Avoid arching your lower back; maintain a neutral spine.
Ensure the dumbbell is secure on your hips to avoid shifting during the exercise.
results.description: Dumbbell Hip Thrust (Version 2) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against a bench, knees bent, and feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell with each hand across your hips.
Press through your heels to lift your hips upward until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Hold the top position for a moment, ensuring your glutes are fully contracted.
Lower your hips back down to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Press through your heels to maximize glute activation.
Avoid arching your lower back; maintain a neutral spine.
Focus on squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
results.description: Dumbbell Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Jumping Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides. Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and core engaged.
Lower yourself into a squat position by bending your knees and hips, keeping your back straight and the dumbbells close to your body.
Explosively push through your heels to jump straight up into the air, extending your legs and keeping the dumbbells by your sides.
Land softly on your forefeet. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees track over your toes during the squat and landing phases to avoid strain on your joints.
Use a controlled motion when landing to minimize impact on your joints.
Keep your chest lifted and your back straight to maintain proper posture.
results.description: Dumbbell Jumping Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Dumbbell Kneeling Hold to Stand Clean Grip
instructions: Begin in a kneeling position on both knees with a dumbbell in each hand, held with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) at shoulder height.

Engage your thighs and bring one foot forward, planting it flat on the floor to form a 90-degree angle with your knee. Press through the planted foot to stand up, bringing your other foot forward to meet it, standing upright.
Lower back into the kneeling position by stepping one foot back and lowering the knee to the floor, followed by the other knee, returning to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, alternating the leading leg if preferred.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned with your ankle to avoid undue stress on the joint.
Move smoothly and controlled, focusing on engaging your glutes and quadriceps during the transition.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise.
results.description: Dumbbell Kneeling Hold to Stand Clean Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Kneeling Squat
instructions: Begin in a kneeling position with both knees on the floor, torso straight upright from knees to shoulders. Holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) at shoulder height.
Bend your knees further pushing your hips backward to sit back onto your heels, keeping your torso upright.
Push your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a controlled motion throughout.
tips: Squeeze your glutes as you push your hips forward to maximize muscle activation.
Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward during the movement.
Use a controlled motion to avoid putting strain on your knees.
results.description: Dumbbell Kneeling Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Lunge Alternating on the Spot
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides.

Take a step forward with your right foot and lower your body into a lunge position by bending both knees. Your right knee should be directly above your right ankle, and your left knee should hover just above the floor.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left leg, alternating legs with each repetition.
tips: Ensure your front knee does not extend past your toes to avoid strain on the knee joint.
Maintain a steady and controlled pace to ensure proper form and balance.
Exhale as you push back to the starting position and inhale as you lower into the lunge.
results.description: Dumbbell Lunge Alternating on the Spot is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Dumbbell Lunge Pulse
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides.

Take a step forward with your right foot and lower your body into a lunge position by bending both knees. Your right knee should be directly above your right ankle, and your left knee should hover just above the floor.
From the lunge position, pulse up and down by slightly raising and lowering your body a few inches for 2-3 pulses. Keeping the movement controlled and small.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position. Repeat the movement with your left leg, alternating legs with each set.
tips: Ensure your front knee does not extend past your toes to avoid strain on the knee joint.
Maintain a steady and controlled pace to ensure proper form and balance.
Exhale as you push back to the starting position and inhale as you lower into the lunge.
results.description: Dumbbell Lunge Pulse is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Dumbbell Lunge to Overhead Press
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing each other.

Step forward with your right foot and lower your body into a lunge position by bending both knees while simultaneously pressing the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended. Your right knee should be directly above your right ankle, and your left knee should hover just above the floor.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position while lowering the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
Repeat the movement with your left leg, alternating legs with each set.
tips: Ensure your front knee does not extend past your toes to avoid strain on the knee joint.
Keep a steady and controlled pace to ensure proper form and balance.
Exhale as you press the dumbbells overhead and inhale as you lower them back down.
results.description: Dumbbell Lunge to Overhead Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Triceps, Calves.

results.name: Dumbbell Narrow Stance Squats
instructions: Stand with your feet close together, about hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your palms facing your body.
Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees to lower your body, keeping the dumbbells at your sides.
Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the floor or as low as you can comfortably go while maintaining proper form.
Push through your heels to stand back up, straightening your legs and returning to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your weight is evenly distributed through your feet, especially your heels, to activate your glutes and quadriceps.
Breathe in as you lower into the squat and breathe out as you push back up.
Keep your knees in line with your toes to avoid excessive strain on your knees.
results.description: Dumbbell Narrow Stance Squats is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Dumbbell Offset Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell against your shoulder with a neutral grip. Extend your opposite arm forward at shoulder height for balance.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat while keeping your chest lifted and your torso facing forward.
Lower until your thighs are approximately parallel to the floor, or as far as you can while keeping your heels down and your knees aligned with your toes.
Press through your heels to stand upright, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions before holding the dumbbell on the opposite side.
tips: Brace your core to prevent your torso from leaning toward the weighted side.
Keep your hips and shoulders level without twisting your body.
Distribute your weight evenly across your heels and the middle of your feet.
Inhale as you lower into the squat and exhale as you return to standing.
results.description: Dumbbell Offset Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core, Obliques.
